# Disney is raising prices for Disney+ and Hulu. See what the streaming services will cost.

 By 

 Mary Cunningham 

Mary Cunningham Reporter, MoneyWatch

 Mary Cunningham 

 September 23, 2026 / 2:59 PM EDT / CBS News 

The Walt Disney Company is raising prices for several of its subscription plans, including Disney+, Hulu and certain bundle options.

Both standalone ad-free plans for Disney+ and Hulu are increasing by $2.50, or 13%, bringing the total cost to $21.49 a month for each, the entertainment giant told CBS News on Wednesday. The cost of Disney+ and Hulu plans with ads will both rise by 50 cents to $12.49 a month. The ad-free plan that bundles the services will also go up by $2 to $21.99.

The company said it will continue pricing its most popular bundle, a joint Disney+/Hulu subscription with ads, at $12.99.

The price hikes for new subscribers take effect immediately, while existing subscribers will see the new billing rates kick in next month. Here's a full breakdown of Disney's new subscription prices:

- Disney+, Hulu Bundle (with ads) unchanged at $12.99 per month
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium (ad-free) is increasing by $2 from $19.99 to $21.99 per month
- Disney+ and Hulu standalone plans (with ads) are increasing by 50 cents from $11.99 to $12.49 per month
- Disney+ and Hulu Premium standalone plans (ad-free) are increasing by $2.50 from $18.99 to $21.49 per month
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle (with ads) is increasing by $2 from $19.99 to $21.99 per month
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle Premium (ad-free) is increasing by $3 from $29.99 to $32.99 per month
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle (with ads) unchanged at $35.99 per month
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle Premium (ad-free) unchanged at $44.99 per month

Last year, Disney announced that it would combine Disney+ and Hulu to create a "unified app experience." Hulu subscribers can now link their profiles and watch history on Disney+, CEO Josh D'Amaro said during the company's earnings call in August. 

Disney also offers bundle plans with ESPN, which it acquired in 1996 as part of its acquisition of Capital Cities/ABC.

 Edited by Alain Sherter

# How Much Does Disney+ Cost?

Disney+ costs $12.49 a month for an ad-based subscription or $21.49 a month for an ad-free experience.

Written by

Lisa Mulka

Tommy Tindall is a lead writer and content strategist covering how to make money — and how to keep it. He’s recorded and written about his experience testing popular gig jobs like driving for Uber, delivering with DoorDash and full-service shopping for Instacart. He loves making an extra buck, but laments the hours of awkward silence he endured as an Uber driver (never again).

Cool kids might call him a content creator because he makes YouTube videos for the NerdWallet channel and app, but he himself is no longer very cool. How is this page expert verified?

NerdWallet's content is fact-checked for accuracy, timeliness and relevance. It undergoes a thorough review process involving writers and editors to ensure the information is as clear and complete as possible.

Disney’s popular streaming service offers a robust library. It ranges from classic animated films and exclusive Marvel content like the new "Wonder Man" series to hit shows like "The Simpsons." 

But just how much does Disney+ cost? It starts at $12.49 a month. 

## How much does a Disney+ subscription cost per month?

The final cost of Disney+ depends on whether you’re willing to put up with ads. 

The ad-supported plan is $12.49 a month. The ad-free Premium plan costs $21.49 a month or $214.99 a year.

That said, Disney+ offers some of the most flexible package deals of any streaming platform. Users can bundle Disney+ with other streaming services for enhanced savings and a larger content menu. Packages include:

- Disney+ (with ads) and Hulu (with ads): $12.99 a month. 
- Disney+ (with ads), Hulu (with ads) and ESPN Select (with ads): $21.99 a month. 
- Disney+ (ad-free) and Hulu (ad-free): $21.99 a month. 
- Disney+ (ad-free), Hulu (ad-free) and ESPN Select (with ads): $32.99 a month.

Some existing subscribers have the “legacy” bundle for $27.99 a month, which combines Disney+ (ad-free), Hulu (with ads) and ESPN Select (with ads). This plan is no longer available for new subscribers.

This tool was created with the assistance of AI. It has been reviewed by our editorial team for accuracy and quality.

## What does Disney+ include?

The ad-supported version of Disney+ includes:

- Disney movies and TV series.
- Star Wars and Marvel content.
- 4K playback (on select titles).
- The ability to stream up to four devices simultaneously.
- A total of seven user profiles.

In addition to ad-free streaming, the premium version also offers:

- Unlimited downloads on up to 10 devices.
- Dolby Atmos sound (on select titles).

## Does Disney+ allow password sharing?

Disney does not allow sharing of accounts or subscriptions outside of a single household, which it defines as devices that are linked to your personal primary residence.

Disney+ and Hulu raise prices by up to 13 percent after doubling profits - Ars Technica

# Disney+ and Hulu raise prices by up to 13 percent after doubling profits 

 The Disney+ ad-free plan is now more expensive than Netflix’s. 

 Scharon Harding – Sep 23, 2026 5:18 pm | 126 

 

 A promotional image for the third season of The Mandalorian. Credit: Disney 

 A promotional image for the third season of The Mandalorian. Credit: Disney 

Disney+ got its fourth price hike in four years today. Hulu prices also went up.

Disney+ and Hulu’s respective standalone, ad-free plans (which also support 4K and HDR) are each increasing 13 percent from $19 per month to $21.50/month.

Disney+ and Hulu’s respective standalone plans with ads increased from $12 to $12.50.

The Walt Disney Company also increased prices for bundles of the streaming services, including those with ESPN.

The price for the Disney+ and Hulu bundle without ads increased from $20/month to $22/month. The Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads ($13) didn’t get more expensive.

However, prices increased for the Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN Select bundles with ads (from $20 to $22) and without ads (from $29 to $33).

Monthly subscription prices for Hulu + Live, which adds cable channels delivered over the Internet to Hulu’s on-demand options, went up by $10.

For comparison, Netflix is currently $9/month with ads and starts at $20/month without ads. There’s also a $27/month ad-free plan for premium features, like 4K. That means Disney+ and Hulu are both more expensive than the most popular streaming service now, unless you want 4K or HDR.

The last time that Disney+ raised prices was in October 2025. It also raised prices in October 2024, October 2023, and December 2022. It launched in 2019.

Hulu’s most recent price hikes occurred in October 2025, October 2024, October 2023, and October 2022. It launched in 2008.

Today’s price hikes follow Disney increasing the price for both tiers of its ESPN streaming service on September 17.

In its most recent quarterly earnings report, Disney reported that revenue from Disney+ and Hulu increased 11 percent. Operating income for Disney+ and Hulu combined increased 116 percent year over year to $712 million. Netflix, for comparison, reported operating income of $4.19 billion in its most recent earnings report. Netflix has many more subscribers (325 million as of January) than Disney+ (131.6 million as of September 2025) and Hulu (59.7 million subscribers for its on-demand streaming service as of September 2025).

Price hikes are likely part of Disney’s ongoing effort at streaming profitability. Netflix’s success shows there is still ample room for growth. The new prices may also steer customers more toward bundles, which streaming service providers believe lead to fewer cancellations and help Disney manage the unpredictable ads market.

 Scharon Harding Senior Technology Reporter 

 Scharon Harding Senior Technology Reporter

# Hulu + Live TV Hits $99.99 as Disney Raises Disney+ and Hulu Prices Again

Founder & Editor · TVLander

TL;DR

Ad-free Disney+ and Hulu now cost $21.49 a month each, but the ad-supported Disney+/Hulu Duo stays at $12.99. Here's every new price and when it hits your bill.

Hulu + Live TV Hits $99.99 as Disney Raises Disney+ and Hulu Prices Again featured image

Prices checked against hulu.com and disneyplus.com on Sep. 25, 2026. U.S. prices.

Hulu + Live TV now costs $99.99 a month in the U.S., up $10. Ad-free Disney+ and ad-free Hulu each jumped to $21.49 a month from $18.99, an increase of about 13%. The new prices took effect for new subscribers on Wednesday, Sep. 23, and already appear on Disney+ and Hulu's own sign-up pages.

One plan didn't move. The ad-supported Disney+/Hulu Duo Basic stays at $12.99 a month, only 50 cents more than Disney+ with Ads or Hulu with Ads on its own ($12.49 each). For most households, that makes it the best value in Disney's lineup.

It's Disney's fourth straight yearly price increase, after rounds in October 2023, October 2024 and October 2025. Disney didn't issue a press release. It updated its help center and confirmed the new prices to CBS News, which reported that the company "will continue pricing its most popular bundle, a joint Disney+/Hulu subscription with ads, at $12.99." The Wall Street Journal also reported the increase, citing a person familiar with the matter.

## When existing subscribers pay more

New subscribers pay the new prices now. Disney's help center says existing subscribers will see the new price in billing cycles on or after Oct. 21, 2026. Variety, MacRumors and Cord Cutters News report that the higher price lands on current customers' next monthly bill. CBS News says it reaches existing subscribers "next month."

For Hulu + Live TV, StreamingBetter reports that existing subscribers will move to the new price on or after Oct. 21, 2026, depending on their billing cycle. Disney hasn't confirmed that date publicly. Last year's increase took effect on Oct. 21, 2025.

The $99.99 plan pairs the live TV lineup with Hulu with Ads, Disney+ with Ads and ESPN Select. The $109.99 Premium plan keeps the same ESPN tier but swaps in ad-free Hulu and Disney+ Premium. # Disney+ and Hulu Prices Rose in the U.S. — What Each Plan Costs Now

Disney+ and Hulu's U.S. ad-free plans now cost $21.49 a month. Compare September 2026 standalone and bundle prices, unchanged tiers, promotions and billing timing.

SA By Sara Avegaard Published September 24, 2026 at 7:08 PM CEST 3 min read

Official Hulu on Disney+ logo showing both streaming brands together. Disney+ Press

Disney+ and Hulu’s U.S. standalone plans now cost $12.49 a month with ads or $21.49 a month for Premium. The ad-free price is $2.50 higher than before; the ad-supported price is up 50 cents. The Disney+/Hulu bundle with ads remains $12.99 a month, while its Premium bundle rose to $21.99. New subscriber prices took effect September 23, 2026. Existing subscribers see the change on their next monthly bill, according to TheWrap’s price-change report.

These are standard U.S. monthly prices, before tax or any eligibility-limited offer. Disney currently advertises lower six-month introductory prices for some bundles; those offers renew at the regular rates shown below.

## What Changed in September 2026?

| U.S. plan | Previous monthly price | Current monthly price | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+ with ads | $11.99 | $12.49 | +$0.50 |
| Disney+ Premium | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Hulu with ads | $11.99 | $12.49 | +$0.50 |
| Hulu Premium | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$2.50 |
| Disney+ + Hulu with ads | $12.99 | $12.99 | No change |
| Disney+ + Hulu Premium | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$2.00 |
| Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN Select with ads | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$2.00 |
| Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN Select Premium | $29.99 | $32.99 | +$3.00 |

The current rates come from Disney’s plan listings and Hulu. Previous rates and the timing of the increase come from contemporaneous reporting. Disney+ Premium also has a current $214.99 annual option; the table compares monthly plans only.

## Which Bundles Stayed the Same?

Disney’s current site still lists Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN Unlimited at $35.99 a month with ads on Disney+ and Hulu, and $44.99 for the Premium Disney+/Hulu combination. Both Unlimited bundle prices were unchanged in the September price-change reporting. ESPN Select and Unlimited are different plans; do not compare their prices as if they contain the same sports access.

The Disney+/Hulu bundle with ads also stayed at $12.99. That is just 50 cents more than either ad-supported service alone at $12.49. The Premium duo at $21.99 is likewise 50 cents more than either $21.49 standalone Premium plan. That is a price comparison, not a claim that every viewer needs both services.

## What About HBO Max and Live TV?

Disney currently lists its Disney+ + Hulu + HBO Max bundle at $21.99 a month with ads or $34.99 without ads. Its Hulu + Live TV package, which includes Disney+ and ESPN Select, is $99.99 a month; the Premium Live TV combination is $109.99. Check the exact included services and any trial or promotion at checkout, because these are different packages from the two-service bundles above.

## When Will Existing Subscribers Pay More?

The September 23 rates applied to new U.S. sign-ups immediately. Existing monthly subscribers do not all get charged on the announcement date: the higher amount appears on their next billing cycle. Check your own account notice and renewal date for the precise charge. These prices do not describe Disney+ or Hulu subscriptions outside the U.S.

Disney’s current bundle page also offers eligible customers six months of the Disney+/Hulu ad-supported duo at $11.99 a month or the Premium duo at $19.99 a month, billed for the full six-month term. After that, they renew at $12.99 and $21.99 a month respectively. Those temporary prices are not the new standard rates.

Short answer: Existing Disney+ subscribers pay the new prices from their first bill on or after October 21, 2026. Premium goes from $18.99 to $21.49 a month. The plan with ads goes from $11.99 to $12.49. Here’s the odd part: the Disney+ and Hulu Premium bundle is $21.99, just 50 cents more than Disney+ Premium alone. The Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads didn’t change at $12.99. If you pay for Premium by itself, the bundle or the ad tier is almost always the better deal now.

A $2.50 bump doesn’t sound like much. Over a year it’s $30, and Disney has now raised Disney+ prices roughly once a year since launch.

But the more interesting change isn’t the hike itself. Disney priced its plans so that Disney+ Premium on its own now looks like a bad deal next to the bundle. Once you see the numbers side by side, the “what should I do before October 21” question mostly answers itself.

Below is every new price, the plan math for the three most common situations, and how to switch or cancel cleanly before your renewal date.

## When does the Disney+ price increase hit existing subscribers?

Existing U.S. Disney+ subscribers are charged the new prices starting with their first billing date on or after October 21, 2026, while new subscribers have paid the higher rates since September 23, 2026, according to Disney’s announcement as reported by CBS News on September 23, 2026.

So the exact day depends on your billing date. If you’re billed on the 5th, your first higher charge lands November 5. If you’re billed on the 22nd, it lands October 22.

That’s useful. Most people have a week or more to decide.

## How much does each Disney+ plan cost now?

As of October 2026, Disney+ Premium costs $21.49 a month and Disney+ with ads costs $12.49 a month in the U.S., up from $18.99 and $11.99, while the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads stays at $12.99 a month, per Disney’s figures reported by CBS News and Variety.

| Disney+ Premium (no ads) | $18.99 | $21.49 | +$30.00 |

| Disney+ and Hulu bundle Premium | $19.99 | $21.99 | +$24.00 |

Prices from Disney’s September 23, 2026 announcement as reported by CBS News and Variety. Yearly change is our calculation (monthly difference × 12), before tax.

## Is the Disney+ and Hulu bundle cheaper than Disney+ Premium alone?

The Disney+ and Hulu Premium bundle costs $21.99 a month after the October 2026 increase, only $0.50 more than Disney+ Premium alone at $21.49, so anyone paying for ad-free Disney+ by itself can add ad-free Hulu for 50 cents.

When I compared the old and new tables, I found that the gap used to be bigger in the other direction. Under the old prices, the Premium bundle cost $1.00 more than Disney+ Premium alone ($19.99 vs $18.99). Now it’s half that.
